source.title: Steering Sparse Autoencoder Latents to Control Dynamic Head Pruning in Vision Transformers (Student Abstract)

record.file_problem: The full student abstract text is present; it includes an appendix and figure descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE latents as a steering tool for dynamic head pruning and reports performance of that method. It does not test superposition, capacity pressure, or whether SAE latents are complete, stable, or canonical units.
record.gate_note: Reported changes in pruning and accuracy under deliberately induced latent steering are outcomes of the study's control method, not evidence that the claim's predicted representations arise without steering. The study is on a ViT, not an LLM. The reported SAE reconstruction and latent-overlap results are recorded as related findings not covered by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains a k-sparse SAE on a ViT-Small final-layer CLS embedding only as a tool to steer dynamic head pruning. It reports that method's accuracy and head-usage outcomes. It does not test superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, or SAE canonicality. V4 names LLMs, and this system is a vision transformer.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Amplifying per-class frequent SAE latents makes final-layer dynamic head pruning controllable and interpretable, revealing class-specific head subsets. The work is limited to the final layer and small datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a k-sparse autoencoder on ViT residual embeddings and steers selected latents to control pruning; it does not use the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with steering strategy (per-class frequent, global frequent, or random) and steering strength α; negative steering chiefly changes head usage for the per-class strategy. The experiments focus on the final layer.

fits_no_version.finding: In the ViT, replacing the final-layer embedding with its SAE reconstruction changes accuracy by −0.12% and head usage by +0.025.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on vision transformer residual embeddings preserve task-relevant information, a vision analogue of V4's dictionary-recovery claim.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latent usage overlaps about 0.38–0.39 for semantically similar class pairs and is near zero for unrelated classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ViTs, SAE latents carry class-level semantic structure.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Student Abstract)
record.problems: The study focuses on one small ViT model, CIFAR-100, and the final layer. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The claim's central superposition and capacity questions are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the deliberately induced steering results: those report the performance of the proposed pruning-control method, not spontaneous behavior predicted by the claim. The SAE training MSE and the baseline pruning accuracy are not measurements of the claim's representation hypotheses.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transition and feature geometry are not examined.
Capacity competition and dedicated dimensions for important features are not examined; no neuron-level polysemanticity is measured.
There is no test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
There are no LLM results. SAE reconstruction fidelity is reported only for a ViT, which is a different kind of system.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality of SAE features are not tested.
There is no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's classification is confirmed. The steering results are deliberately induced and are the study's own method, so they are rightly left out as rows. One further related number is unrecorded: overlap between global and per-class frequent latents is 0.1641, which the authors read as class-discriminative concepts. It bears on no version. All results are single-run with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The study does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemantic neurons.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The study uses a vision transformer, not an LLM; it does not test feature spread across LLM neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features or test the geometry of superposed directions.

rows.note: This reports reconstruction fidelity for pruning, not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
